summary: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded planes for over four hours—the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years—after new technology overloaded antiquated air traffic control equipment, causing "intermittent" communications and radar gaps.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a contractor replacing copper wires with fiber optic lines caused the system overload; he and the White House are pushing for $30 billion more to complete critical infrastructure upgrades.
The stoppage affected about a quarter of 45,000 daily U.S. flights, with more than 4,100 cancellations. Aviation consultant Andrew Charlton said the "knock-on effect" of the disruption is incredible.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said Saturday that U.S. air travel should be fully recovered by the end of tomorrow, though flights will still experience delays and cancellations throughout the day.

Modernizing active aviation systems is "incredibly complex and dangerous," aviation consultant Andrew Charlton warned, as officials investigate potential contractor "incompetence" while aging equipment remains a long-term concern.
title: Source Icon

summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the Alaska governor's race following a week of vote counting, the Associated Press reported. The 37-year-old replaces term-limited Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy, who has served since 2018.

In Alaska's ranked-choice system, Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republicans, including one backed by President Trump. The field featured Bernadette Wilson, Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson, and Alaska Attorney General Treg Taylor.

Known as JKT, the incoming governor campaigned on a "high-energy, bipartisan, problem-solving approach." He secured endorsements from former governors and Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski while describing himself as a "man of the middle."
With this victory, Democrats will hold 30 governors' offices nationwide, up from 24. Kreiss-Tomkins becomes the first Democrat to lead the state since Tony Knowles left office in 2002.

Assuming office Dec 7, Kreiss-Tomkins faces rising costs for food and fuel alongside a looming natural gas shortage. Alaskans have also migrated out of the state for over a decade, presenting long-term challenges.
title: Alaska elects Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, the first Democrat governor since 1998

summary: According to the White House, President Donald Trump will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, on November 19 for an unprecedented trilateral summit on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

Assistant Press Secretary Olivia Wales stated that Trump intends to focus the discussions on nuclear arms control and reducing global nuclear stockpiles, following the expiration of the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty earlier in the year.

A senior U.S. administration official noted that Washington views China's rapidly expanding nuclear arsenal as a central reason for bringing Beijing into arms control talks, while cautioning that the summit is intended as an initial conversation rather than a forum expected to produce an immediate formal agreement.

According to administration officials, Trump also plans to discuss the conflict with Iran during the three-way sit-down, though Russia's war against Ukraine will not be explicitly on the agenda because Washington and Moscow are addressing that conflict on a separate diplomatic track that does not involve Beijing.

Before the trilateral session, Trump is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting and working lunch with Xi Jinping, while the White House confirmed that Trump and Putin will not hold a separate one-on-one meeting during the trip.
title: Trump to meet with China’s Xi and Russia’s Putin at historic trilateral sit-down on nuclear non-proliferation

summary: On Friday, the 520-foot tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with the docked 295-foot riverboat American Heritage in New Orleans at 12:30 p.m., partially submerging the vessel and sending passengers into the Mississippi River.

Local officials and river pilots suggest the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker experienced a steering failure before striking the paddlewheel riverboat, though Port of New Orleans authorities maintain the exact cause remains under investigation.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno called the rescue a "miracle on the Mississippi," noting that all 129 passengers and crew were accounted for, though 32 people were transported to local hospitals with noncritical injuries.
Following the collision, the U.S. Coast Guard closed the Mississippi River to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 to facilitate rescue operations and damage assessment.
Echoing the 1996 Bright Field crash, the National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation to determine the collision's circumstances as crews work to reopen the critical waterway.
title: Over 30 injured, no one missing after tanker collides with riverboat in New Orleans: Officials

summary: On Friday, The Associated Press projected Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated Republican Representative Lauren Boebert in Colorado's 4th Congressional District, with Laubacher securing 48.8% of the vote.
Following a shift to the Republican-heavy 4th District in 2024, Boebert faced ethics complaints alleging staff relationships, which she denied as "utterly false."
With a 1% margin separating the candidates after 10 days of tabulation, Laubacher's victory leaves Democrats with a 7-1 majority among Colorado's House seats.
While Boebert refused to concede, citing ongoing counts of military and overseas ballots, Laubacher arrived in Washington on Monday for New Member Orientation with the 120th Congress.
The loss concludes Boebert's six-year congressional career, as Democrats flipped this Trump+18 district amid their sweeping midterm victories across the nation.
title: GOP Rep. Lauren Boebert will lose reelection to Democrat Eileen Laubacher in Colorado, AP projects

summary: On Saturday, U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a temporary restraining order blocking the Trump administration from closing East Potomac Park and East Potomac Golf Course on Sunday, preserving public access through November 28, 2026.

President Donald Trump planned to close the course for a 15-month renovation into a "World Championship Public Facility," but preservationists and local golfers sued in February, arguing the project violates federal environmental laws and threatens public access.

Judge Reyes found the administration's stated safety justifications "pretextual" and determined the government violated federal law "to meet an arbitrary deadline" by failing to solicit required public comment before closure.

The order requires the government "cannot use the absence of golf operations as a reason to exclude the public," though the Justice Department vowed it will "always vociferously defend" the administration's agenda in court.

Reyes appointed former U.S. Attorney Jessie Liu to investigate whether government officials misled the court, an inquiry reflecting institutional strain as legal battles over Trump's capital renovation projects intensify.
title: Federal judge temporarily blocks Trump administration from closing East Potomac Park

summary: On Friday, the Port of New Orleans sued the owners of the Atlantic Asphalt tanker, which struck the docked American Heritage cruise ship and caused more than $1 million in damage to the Thalia Street Terminal.

The tanker appeared to lose steering control before striking the cruise ship, forcing 197 passengers and crew into the Mississippi River; officials hailed the rescue effort as a "miracle on the Mississippi."

District Judge Wendy Vitter authorized the tanker's seizure Friday, enabling the port's legal claim. Thirty-two people were hospitalized with non-critical injuries, though no fatalities were reported.

Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said crews must remove 16,000 gallons of fuel from the partially submerged cruise ship. The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation into the crash.

Thome Ship Management stated Saturday the tanker is stable at anchor and the firm is "fully complying with the local authorities as they carry out the necessary investigations." Traffic on the Mississippi River remains limited but should resume soon.
title: New Orleans port sues to get control of tanker that crashed into cruise ship on Mississippi River

summary: A UPS Boeing 767 and a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 collided while taxiing at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, with the Copa flight having just arrived from Panama City.
Air traffic control audio captured the UPS Flight 358 pilot saying, "Somebody hit us," before acknowledging, "Yeah we went too far and he clipped us with his wing" during the taxiway incident.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue reported no major injuries, though Fox Sports journalist Andy Slater noted two people aboard the Copa flight complained of back pain as airport operations continued without disruption.

The collision occurred as Miami International Airport continues experiencing delays following Friday's nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop that disrupted travel for about 1.5 million passengers.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford stated Saturday that the national air travel schedule should return to normal by the end of Sunday, despite more than 800 flights scheduled for Sunday being canceled nationwide.
title: UPS plane, Copa Airlines jet collide at Miami International Airport, officials say

summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced that U.S. air travel should largely return to normal schedules by late Sunday, following a nationwide flight shutdown that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours on Friday.
Officials traced the disruption to FAA contractor L3Harris, which installed a faulty router at a remote facility that triggered data overloading across 17 of the agency's 22 en route centers.

Airlines canceled more than 5,300 flights and delayed almost 6,300 on Saturday. Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, and American Airlines each canceled about 25 percent of their flights, while JetBlue canceled nearly 45 percent.

Representatives Rick Larsen and Andre Carson, slated to chair the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee next year, vowed to hold the administration accountable. They noted the Transportation Department only spent $1 billion of the $12.5 billion received last year.

Secretary Duffy called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade air traffic control systems on Friday, an increase from his earlier $30 billion request. House Speaker Mike Johnson stated on Saturday that he supports approving additional funding this year.
title: US air travel disruptions to persist until late on Sunday, FAA head says

Alaska's vote counting continues following the November 13 deadline for mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day, explaining why the close contest remains uncalled nearly a week after polls closed.

Statistical analysis shows Sullivan faces a steep hurdle, requiring roughly 93% of redistributed votes to overcome the deficit, while ballot exhaustion limits the available pool as over 45% of voters ranked neither candidate.
Alaska Division of Elections officials are scheduled to run the ranked-choice tabulation on November 18, which also serves as the final deadline for receiving absentee ballots.

A victory for Peltola would secure a 56-44 Senate majority for Democrats next year, though the contest remains the final uncalled 2026 Senate race with the NBC News Decision Desk maintaining at least 95% confidence.
title: Democrat Mary Peltola is likely to win Alaska’s Senate race, as vote counting continues: NBC News

summary: On Saturday, U.S. diesel prices fell below $6 a gallon to $5.998, according to GasBuddy, marking the first time in two months the national average retreated from that threshold.
Easing geopolitical tensions and seasonal demand weakness reduced fuel market pressure, as Brent crude futures dropped 18.5% over the past two weeks.

The Trump administration launched an $8 billion support program for farmers and expanded access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, while refinery maintenance largely completed by November allowed production to recover.
Diesel prices had previously peaked at $6.519 in September, driven by supply disruptions from the US-Israeli conflict with Iran and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries.
Gasoline prices also fell below $4 per gallon this month for the first time since August 10, according to GasBuddy data, reflecting broader market relief.
title: US diesel below $6 a gallon at 2-month low on easing tensions, weaker demand

summary: On Friday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced he struck a deal with President Donald Trump to delay enforcement of new federal food-stocking requirements for 90 days, extending relief nationwide to small retailers risking SNAP authorization loss.

Mamdani urged the USDA to postpone the rules after neighborhood bodegas warned they lacked sufficient time to comply; updated standards now require stores to stock 84 items across four categories including dairy, grains, protein, and produce.

For many bodegas, SNAP purchases account for up to 30% of typical sales, making these stores essential for more than one million New Yorkers and 36 million Americans who rely on the program for affordable food.

City Hall will work with the Department of Small Business Services and the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to help owners identify inventory gaps and connect with distributors carrying qualifying products during the extension.

Uncertainty remains regarding when the final enforcement deadline will fall, as it is unclear how the 90-day extension affects the broader reauthorization review process for the city's more than 10,000 bodegas with limited shelf space.
title: Mamdani announces deal with White House for 90-day extension for new SNAP requirements

The South Carolina Arms Collector Association was hosting the event at the venue, which the Shriners own and frequently rent for public markets and gatherings.

Authorities have not publicly identified the deputy or the deceased gunman; drivers are urged to avoid the area around Jamil and St. Andrews roads during the investigation.
Emergency services were dispatched to the scene, according to Lexington County SC Firewire, where show rules prohibit attendees from carrying loaded weapons except for on-duty police officers.
title: Deputy Working Security at South Carolina Gun Show Fatally Shoots Customer Who Shot Him

summary: On Friday, the tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with the American Cruise Lines paddle-wheeler American Heritage on the Mississippi River in New Orleans , forcing 191 people aboard to evacuate as the vessel sank.
First responders pulled about 100 people from the water, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said Saturday, with 32 individuals transported to local hospitals on Friday following the collision.
Nine people remained hospitalized on Saturday afternoon, Moreno said, while the National Transportation Safety Board deployed 16 investigators on-site to interview those involved in the incident.
The NTSB recovered the voyage data recorder from the Atlantic Asphalt on Saturday, which documents the tanker's speed, course, and bridge audio to help determine the collision's cause.
Removing the sunken American Heritage from the river could take weeks, Mayor Moreno confirmed, though officials verified that no one was killed in the collision.
title: Data recorder recovered from tanker in New Orleans cruise ship collision, NTSB says

summary: Jared Kushner, President Trump's special envoy, announced Saturday that the United States is facilitating direct engagement between Moscow and European partners to secure a peace deal in the Ukraine war.

Kushner and Steve Witkoff held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy this past week, following the first round of U.S.-brokered talks since February.
Zelenskyy warned Friday that Moscow could use security framework discussions to weaken NATO and reshape European borders, stating, "In my view, this can be dangerous."
European leaders stressed that security decisions must be made by Europeans themselves, warning against allowing Russia to dictate terms or negotiate NATO's future.
Kushner added Saturday that lasting peace requires security guarantees for Kyiv and "detailed, actionable postwar security arrangements that reduce the risk of another war.
title: U.S. facilitating direct engagement between Europe and Russia amid push for peace in Ukraine, Kushner says

summary: On Saturday, state and federal officers finished searching the BioUrja ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, after a device deemed a "credible threat" was discovered on Friday near the facility.
The incident began Friday when the BioUrja plant notified police of a bomb threat, prompting officials to order residents within a 1-mile radius to evacuate as a precaution.
Personnel from the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives searched the sprawling facility, which Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said spans 44-1/2 football fields.
The Peoria Police Department announced on Facebook that nothing "of concern" was found, allowing authorities to lift the evacuation notice for Peoria's approximately 110,000 residents on Saturday.
Bomb technicians rendered the device safe, though Peoria Police Chief Dixon said an "extensive criminal investigation" is underway to identify the person responsible for the threat.
title: Law enforcement searches Illinois plant after 'credible threat' of explosive device

summary: On Saturday, SpaceX successfully caught its Starship upper stage using giant mechanical arms at Starbase, Texas, after the spacecraft, Ship 42, completed 14 orbits over a 22-hour flight.

SpaceX fell short of its goal to recover both rocket stages when the Super Heavy booster aborted its landing attempt Friday due to a low-fuel alarm, resulting in an offshore splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico.
Deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites, Ship 42 returned to be secured by the launch tower's mechanical 'chopstick' arms, which SpaceX commentator Dan Huot called "the missing link" of spaceflight.

This midair capture serves as a major proof of concept for the Starship program, marking the first time an orbital upper stage has been fully recovered—essential to SpaceX's goal of fully reusable rocket systems.

NASA's Artemis lunar missions and eventual Mars exploration will rely on Starship technology, as SpaceX aims to increase launch cadence to support a constellation of up to one million satellites for orbital data infrastructure.
title: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first

summary: On Friday, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said he is prioritizing inflation trends to guide future interest-rate decisions, noting persistent price pressures remain the primary signal for monetary policy.
Jefferson recently joined 10 Fed policymakers who voted at their October meeting to await further data before considering rate increases, with 2 dissenting from the majority position.

Fed policymakers have indicated in recent weeks that elevated inflation may necessitate larger rate hikes than the single quarter-point increase delivered in September, potentially arriving in quicker succession.

Regarding artificial intelligence, Jefferson said the technology could boost productivity substantially but risks displacing workers faster than they can adapt, limiting monetary policy's ability to address structural employment shifts.

Jefferson emphasized that while AI adoption could increase borrowing costs economy-wide, "Monetary policy can affect cyclical conditions" but cannot address the structural factors determining long-run employment rates.
title: Fed's Jefferson says he is taking his policy cues from inflation

summary: On Friday, a Workday outage locked employees across 11,500 businesses out of their HR accounts, preventing users from clocking in or out, requesting time off, and accessing benefit information.
Workday placed its system into maintenance mode after discovering an issue during backup system testing, causing inconsistent information that could trigger errors when users access accounts.
High-Profile clients including Target, Walmart, and Netflix rely on the platform, alongside the Department of Energy and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory at the California Institute of Technology.

Downdetector recorded nearly 3,000 outage reports shortly after 5 p.m. Friday; a Workday spokesperson said, "Some of our customers are experiencing a service disruption and we're working urgently to investigate and resolve the issue."
Workday has not provided an estimate for platform restoration, leaving employees unable to access benefits enrollment during the outage.
title: Workday, software company with thousands of Fortune 500 clients, joins Microsoft in experiencing major outage

summary: On Wednesday, NASA 's Voyager 1 reached the milestone of one light-day from Earth, having travelled more than 16 billion miles since its 1977 launch. Radio signals from the spacecraft now take 24 hours to reach Earth.
Launched 49 years ago, the probe swept past Jupiter and Saturn in 1979 and 1980 before exiting the solar system. It reached interstellar space—the expansive region between star systems—in 2012.

A skeleton team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, California, sends commands weekly to maintain the plutonium-powered spacecraft. Project manager Suzanne Dodd credits their expertise for keeping Voyager 1 chugging along like "the little engine that could."

Equipped with a gold-plated record carrying greetings in 55 languages, Voyager serves as Earth's ambassador into deep space. In 1990, it captured the iconic "Pale Blue Dot" photograph from beyond Neptune, humanity's most distant portrait of home.

NASA projects another 18,000 years before Voyager 1 completes a full light-year journey, while its twin Voyager 2 will not reach the one light-day milestone until 2035. Project manager Dodd calls the mission "a national treasure.
title: NASA’s Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for a new distance record

The BioUrja facility spans approximately 44-and-a-half football fields and contains ethanol and highly combustible types of chemicals, prompting officials to treat the discovery with extreme caution.
Bomb technicians rendered the device safe at 9:12 p.m. Friday, while the response forced the closure of Interstate 74 and displaced more than 5,000 residents and workers.
Authorities lifted the evacuation order Saturday at 1 p.m. after an exhaustive search revealed no additional hazards, allowing residents and businesses to return.

summary: Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk warned on Saturday that Nvidia could lose critical supply agreements following co-founder Jensen Huang 's resignation, citing the importance of his personal relationships with suppliers and business partners.

Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid mounting scrutiny over alleged relationships with Nvidia Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell and Alice Huang, a businesswoman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence.

Musk said many of Nvidia's supply chain deals were built on personal handshakes with Jensen rather than written contracts. "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost," he added.

Following Huang's resignation, Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. Musk publicly backed a petition on Friday seeking Jensen's reinstatement, stating it "would be an honor" to work with him.

Jensen led Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into a leading supplier of AI chips. His departure creates uncertainty for the company's central role in supplying advanced semiconductors worldwide.

summary: On Friday, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin interrupted a reporter during a briefing on the unprecedented nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop to correct the use of the term "artificial intelligence," insisting on "super intelligence."

Following an executive order, President Donald Trump mandated the term "super intelligence" across federal agencies, reportedly claiming Chinese President Xi Jingping supported the rebranding, despite the original term remaining on the White House web site.

The FAA cited "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety" for the stoppage, which caused more than 10,000 delays and more than 1,700 cancellations by early Friday evening as officials investigated the communications outage.

summary: On Saturday, the Emanuel Nine Memorial opens to the public at Mother Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church in Charleston, South Carolina , honoring nine Bible study attendees killed in 2015.
Established in 1818, Mother Emanuel became a historic site of resistance before a white supremacist fatally shot nine worshippers during Bible study on June 17, 2015.
Architect Michael Arad, designer of the 9/11 Memorial in New York City, created the $20 million site featuring a Fountain of Grace and marble Fellowship Benches, funded primarily through donations.
Sharon Risher, whose mother Ethel Lance was killed, visited the site and stated she wants people to understand the victims' impact endures beyond forgiveness conversations.

The Mother Emanuel Memorial Foundation will launch the Crossroads Education and Outreach program to foster discussions on confronting racism, while a Survivors' Garden honoring five survivors is soon to come.
title: Memorial opens honoring victims of the 2015 Charleston church massacre

summary: Alaska voters rejected Ballot Measure 2 on November 3, marking the second time in two years that Alaskans declined to repeal the state's open primaries and ranked-choice voting system.
Since its 2020 adoption, the system has faced consistent opposition from the Alaska Republican Party and President Donald Trump, who called the method "disastrous and very fraudulent."

Supporters raised $10.4 million to defend the system, significantly outpacing the $2.5 million raised by the measure's campaign, while proponents argue it promotes bipartisanship in the Alaska Legislature.
This month's result ensures Alaskans will continue using the open primary and ranked-choice system through the 2028 election cycle, when Republican U.S. Sen. Lisa Murkowski faces reelection.
Though undecided on timelines, activists including Phil Izon, sponsor of the 2024 initiative, and campaign manager Bethany Marcum have indicated they may launch another repeal effort before 2028.
title: Alaska voters reject ballot measure seeking to repeal open primaries, ranked voting system

summary: Washington University researchers found a blood test detecting a toxic protein can identify advanced CTE, a condition currently only diagnosable after death.
Scientists stumbled onto the potential biomarker while studying Alzheimer, discovering that levels of the protein were also elevated in patients with advanced CTE.
The test achieved an AUC of 0.97 for detecting advanced CTE, though accuracy dropped to 0.64 for early-stage disease according to findings published late Friday in JAMA.
Rudolph Castellani, a neuropathologist at Northwestern University, cautioned the findings remain preliminary and require larger studies, noting the test cannot distinguish CTE from Alzheimer alone.
If validated, the test could allow doctors to diagnose CTE in living patients, potentially facilitating clinical trials for treatments currently limited by the inability to confirm diagnosis.
title: Washington University Study Links Blood Biomarker to Advanced CTE

summary: On Friday, 570 fans dressed as Rocky Balboa gathered at the Philadelphia Museum of Art steps, setting a Guinness World Record for the largest such assembly and surpassing the previous mark of 250.
Rocky Season marks 50 years since the 1976 film written by Sylvester Stallone , a citywide celebration honoring the underdog boxer who became the highest-grossing sports film of its era.

Participants donned the character's signature gray sweatsuits, black beanies, and boxing gloves to achieve the record. "It's going to be awesome just to be a part of history," attendee Kevin Yacovetti said.
On Saturday, tourism officials said 45,000 runners from all 50 states and 75 countries will participate in a "Rocky Run" throughout Philadelphia. The event honors the fictional boxer citywide.
The city organized diverse events this month, including release of Stallone's memoir "The Steps" and a statue rededication, expanding on the inaugural 2023 Rocky Day and subsequent Rocky Fest.
title: 50 years after iconic film, a gathering of ‘Rocky’ fans in Philadelphia breaks a world record
